title: Privacy, Security and AI Governance Competitive Landscape

scope.description: PrivacyPerfect as the reference company, six direct software alternatives, two adjacent platforms and one operating-method substitute. Compare scope, implementation effort, expert support, record reuse and accountable reviews.
scope.inclusionLogic: Include alternatives that can serve the same privacy/security/supplier/AI governance buying decision or materially substitute existing enterprise workflows. Cookiebot and filerskeepers are treated as partners at the boundary, not full-domain competitors.
notes: Public capability descriptions were checked on 2026-09-06. Vendor claims are not independently audited.
HQ follows an official location or legal notice; regions are qualitative market-context judgments, not proof of availability or residency.
The few statistics preserve their reported unit, date and scope. Fortune 500 adoption, platform users and an advertised subscription price are not comparable measures of market share.
Empty businessStats means no sufficiently useful comparable metric was established in this research, not zero revenue or customers.
Direct means overlapping customer jobs, not identical module depth. ServiceNow and Purview are partial substitutes with broader platform scopes.
No competitor logo or source-code evidence is fabricated. Dedicated adviser packaging, architecture and staffing remain modeled assumptions.

players.name: PrivacyPerfect
players.description: Reference company for this domain. Its four solution areas connect privacy, information security, supplier and AI governance, with expert support. The relevant strategic question is whether shared records and approachable contribution create durable value for European organizations; this is a hypothesis, not a measured competitive advantage.

businessStats.scope: Vortex investment event; not revenue, valuation or current growth
Advertised SME package; tax treatment, contract terms and current availability require confirmation

players.name: OneTrust
players.description: Broad governance platform covering privacy automation, technology risk, third parties and AI. It competes for buyers seeking an integrated program and a wider integration ecosystem. Compare a scoped pilot, operating effort and module packaging before inferring that breadth will improve this organization’s review outcomes.

businessStats.scope: Company-reported Fortune 500 use of OneTrust across its offer, not privacy-module market share or total customer count

players.name: TrustArc
players.description: Privacy management software and services alternative for organizations building repeatable privacy operations. It belongs in the same privacy-program shortlist; compare assessment support, record reuse, rights workflows and specialist service scope using current demonstrations rather than assuming identical coverage across every AI or security feature.

players.name: DataGuard
players.description: European security and compliance offering combining software with expert support. Its privacy, security, supplier and assessment surfaces make it relevant to organizations that need both tools and specialist capacity. Test the division of responsibility between customer, software and adviser, plus service cost and evidence portability.

players.name: Dastra
players.description: Privacy software with customizable workflows, imports, exports and documented integration interfaces. It is relevant where governance teams prioritize adaptable data structures and business collaboration. Compare the effort to configure useful forms and preserve review quality as local customization grows.

players.categoryRelevance: Analytical inclusion category; no measured market-share ranking is implied.

players.name: Responsum
players.description: European privacy, security, risk and AI governance platform with configurable workflows and human-reviewed AI assistance. It is a close regional alternative for the combined domain. Compare client confidentiality, migration support, contributor experience and the controls around suggested changes using realistic records.

players.name: ISMS.online
players.description: Information security and multi-framework assurance platform combining guidance, controls, evidence and review workflows. It competes most directly for the security-management buying decision and also addresses privacy and AI governance. Compare evidence scope, audit handoff and ongoing control-review effort rather than treating certification as a platform guarantee.

players.name: ServiceNow GRC
players.description: Enterprise GRC, integrated risk, third-party risk and privacy workflows within a broader enterprise platform. It can substitute for a specialist governance workspace where the customer already runs shared service workflows. Compare incremental integration value with implementation effort; company-wide software scale is not a measure of this product domain.

players.name: Microsoft Purview
players.description: Data security, governance and compliance capabilities across an enterprise data estate. It may supply technical controls and data context as well as absorb governance budget, especially in an existing Microsoft environment. Treat it as a partial substitute and potential integration source; verify which human case and review workflows still need a dedicated workspace.

players.name: Spreadsheets, Email and External Counsel
players.description: Modeled baseline alternative: the organization coordinates records and advice using existing office tools and professional help. It can be adequate for a small, stable scope. The platform must prove lower coordination burden, more reliable ownership or better evidence; software purchase alone does not create compliance. EDPB guidance establishes accountability responsibilities, not an endorsement of this tool combination.
